Topics · Meaning and purpose

How should I treat people of other faiths?

Four things: kindness and fairness, no insult to what others revere, the best way of speaking, no compulsion.

Part 1 of 4

﴿لَّا يَنْهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَـٰتِلُوكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَـٰرِكُمْ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمْ وَتُقْسِطُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allāh loves those who act justly.

Quran · Al-Mumtahanah 60:8

Translation

“If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again. If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him. You shall surely help him with it.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֶ֖נּוּ לֽוֹ׃ כִּֽי־תִרְאֶ֞ה חֲמ֣וֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ֗ רֹבֵץ֙ תַּ֣חַת מַשָּׂא֔וֹ וְחָדַלְתָּ֖ מֵעֲזֹ֣ב ל֑וֹ עָזֹ֥ב תַּעֲזֹ֖ב עִמּֽוֹ׃

the Torah (Exodus) · 23:4-5

World English Bible

The verse begins with what is not forbidden: toward those who have not fought you over religion or driven you from your homes, you are not forbidden to deal kindly and fairly. It closes by saying God loves the fair. So the starting point with a neighbour of a different faith is kindness and fairness, not wariness or coldness. This describes what is permitted and loved, not a restriction. The rule is plain: be fair to those who have done you no harm.

A question for you

Think of a neighbour who does not share your faith. Which is nearest to how you deal with them?

If you sayI keep a polite distance
ThenA polite distance is not forbidden. But the verse names something warmer: kindness and fairness, and says God loves it.
If you sayI deal with kindness and fairness
ThenThat is what the verse describes. It does not ask you to excel at it, only says it is loved.
If you sayI hope they will see things as I do
ThenHope is fine. The verse puts fairness first, whatever happens to your hope. The next verses speak to the way of such hope.

Part 2 of 4

﴿وَلَا تَسُبُّوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَسُبُّوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَدْوًۢا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ ۗ كَذَٰلِكَ زَيَّنَّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمْ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِم مَّرْجِعُهُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not insult those they invoke other than Allāh, lest they insult Allāh in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:108

A guide, on finding a man who has lost his way, brings him back to the right path—he does not mock and jeer at him and then take himself off. You also must show the unlearned man the truth, and you will see that he will follow. But so long as you do not show it him, you should not mock, but rather feel your own incapacity.

Stoic writings · Golden Sayings 63

Epictetus, Golden Sayings (Crossley)

The verse asks for something specific: do not insult what others besides you call on, or the insult will come back upon what you hold most dear, in anger and without knowledge. The logic is simple: whoever insults what a person holds dear will be heard no further, and the insult will be returned. The verse adds that to every nation its own deeds were made to seem fair, meaning every community finds what it holds beautiful. So mocking what anyone holds sacred is out, even where you disagree.

A question for you

When you disagree with someone, how do you speak of what they hold sacred?

If you sayI say nothing about it
ThenSilence is a form of respect, and the verse is content with it. The next verse opens another door: how to speak when you do want to speak.
If you sayI ask them about it
ThenA sincere question builds what mockery tears down. It is close to what the next verse opens.
If you sayI say what I think
ThenSaying what you think is not forbidden. What is asked is that it not be insult. The difference between an opinion and an insult is what the next verse speaks to.

Part 3 of 4

﴿وَلَا تُجَـٰدِلُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ ۖ وَقُولُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَأُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَإِلَـٰهُنَا وَإِلَـٰهُكُمْ وَٰحِدٌ وَنَحْنُ لَهُۥ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, "We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."

Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:46

Translation

The Lord’s servant must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient, in gentleness correcting those who oppose him. Perhaps God may give them repentance leading to a full knowledge of the truth,

Original · Ancient Greek

δοῦλον δὲ κυρίου οὐ δεῖ μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ ἤπιον εἶναι πρὸς πάντας, διδακτικόν, ἀνεξίκακον, ἐν πραΰτητι παιδεύοντα τοὺς ἀντιδιατιθεμένους, μήποτε δώῃ αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς μετάνοιαν εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας,

2 Timothy · 2:24-25

World English Bible

﴿ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَٱلْمَوْعِظَةِ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ ۖ وَجَـٰدِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ ۖ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:125

Translation

Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom.

Original · Ancient Greek

Τίς σοφὸς καὶ ἐπιστήμων ἐν ὑμῖν; δειξάτω ἐκ τῆς καλῆς ἀναστροφῆς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἐν πραΰτητι σοφίας.

James · 3:13

World English Bible

The first verse speaks, in the first place, to those who hold an earlier Book: argue only in the best way, and say that our God and your God is one. The second sets the manner for every invitation: wisdom, good counsel, and arguing in the best way. Winning the argument is not what is asked. The best manner is asked, and the judgment is left to God, who knows best who is guided.

A question for you

Which of these is nearest to “the best way” of talking?

If you sayTo win
ThenWinning is tempting, and neither verse mentions it. They make the aim something else: that the manner be the best.
If you sayTo be understood
ThenThat is close: wisdom and good counsel aim for the words to arrive. One more step remains: that you understand too.
If you sayTo understand them
ThenWhoever understands first is understood more. That is what makes arguing in the best way possible.

Part 4 of 4

﴿لَآ إِكْرَاهَ فِى ٱلدِّينِ ۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَىِّ ۚ فَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِٱلطَّـٰغُوتِ وَيُؤْمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱسْتَمْسَكَ بِٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَا ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

There shall be no compulsion in [acceptance of] the religion. The right course has become distinct from the wrong. So whoever disbelieves in ṭāghūt[104] and believes in Allāh has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And Allāh is Hearing and Knowing.

Translator's notes

[104] False objects of worship, such as idols, heavenly bodies, spirits, human beings, etc.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:256

Translation

But I was willing to do nothing without your consent, that your goodness would not be as of necessity, but of free will.

Original · Ancient Greek

χωρὶς δὲ τῆς σῆς γνώμης οὐδὲν ἠθέλησα ποιῆσαι, ἵνα μὴ ὡς κατὰ ἀνάγκην τὸ ἀγαθόν σου ᾖ ἀλλὰ κατὰ ἑκούσιον·

Philemon · 1:14

World English Bible

﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لَـَٔامَنَ مَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعًا ۚ أَفَأَنتَ تُكْرِهُ ٱلنَّاسَ حَتَّىٰ يَكُونُوا۟ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed - all of them entirely. Then, [O Muḥammad], would you compel the people in order that they become believers?

Quran · Yunus 10:99

Translation

shepherd the flock of God which is among you, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion, but voluntarily; not for dishonest gain, but willingly;

Original · Ancient Greek

ποιμάνατε τὸ ἐν ὑμῖν ποίμνιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐπισκοποῦντες μὴ ἀναγκαστῶς ἀλλὰ ἑκουσίως κατὰ θεόν, μηδὲ αἰσχροκερδῶς ἀλλὰ προθύμως,

1 Peter · 5:2

World English Bible

The first verse says it flatly: no compulsion in religion. The second asks its own Messenger whether he would force people into belief. It says that had God willed, everyone on earth would have believed. That leaves no room for forcing belief. Faith taken by force is not faith. People holding power have at times used force, in many faiths and many lands, and the verse does not take their side, whoever they are.

A question for you

Can faith be forced? And what becomes of it if it is?

If you sayIt becomes form without a heart
ThenThat is close to the argument of the two verses: faith is an act of the heart, and cannot be taken.
If you sayIt hardens and resists
ThenMany experiences teach this: what is imposed breeds a reaction. There is wisdom in that, and it supports the verse.
If you sayIt can become real later
ThenIt can happen, but that does not justify compulsion. The verse protects the heart at the first moment, before it returns on its own.

The same in the other books

Translation

For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same? If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?

the Gospel (Matthew) · 5:46-47

James · 3:17-18

World English Bible

Translation

“‘If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you in your land, you shall not do him wrong.
